Test Case Name: USA Website Timezone is Set to a Valid US Timezone
Admin / Storefront Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Locale Options > Timezone
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin

2. Go to Stores > Configuration

3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view

4. Open General > General > Locale Options

5. Read the Timezone dropdown value
Expected Result: Timezone contains "America/" prefix (e.g. America/Chicago, America/New_York). Must NOT contain "Australia/".
Why It Matters: Wrong timezone causes incorrect order timestamps and scheduling for US customers.

Test Case Name: Locale Language & Format is Set to United States English (en_US)
Admin / Storefront Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Locale Options > Locale
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin

2. Go to Stores > Configuration

3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view

4. Open General > General > Locale Options

5. Read the Locale dropdown value
Expected Result: Locale = en_US (English - United States). Must NOT be en_AU.
Why It Matters: AU locale formats dates as DD/MM/YYYY and changes number/currency formatting. US B2B customers expect MM/DD/YYYY.

Test Case Name: Store Address State is a Valid US State (Not an Australian State)

Test Steps:

3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view

Test Case Name: Base Currency and Default Display Currency are Both Configured as USD (Not AUD)

Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin

2. Go to Stores > Configuration

3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view

4. Open General > Currency Setup > Currency Options

5. Read Base Currency dropdown

6. Read Default Display Currency dropdown
Expected Result: Base Currency = "US Dollar (USD)". Default Display Currency = "US Dollar (USD)". Neither must contain "AUD".
